content: First end-to-end pass through all five real plugins (orchestrate -> plan -> make -> check -> reflect-and-seed) on an actual task, not a synthetic no-op: claim a queued seed, plan one concrete step, execute it, verify against the plan's own stated criteria via a real command (git status --short, not a self-report), then close. The five contracts composed cleanly with no friction or reinterpretation needed between phases -- each role's own run.*.asset.md was sufficient on its own to know what to read from the previous phase and what to write to its own file. The task itself was deliberately small (a .gitignore for build artifacts) so the cycle mechanics, not the task's own difficulty, were what got exercised.
